items.followUp: What is meant by the moment of a couple?

rubric.why: A couple consists of two forces that are equal in magnitude, opposite in direction and parallel.
rubric.description: Identifies the forces in a couple.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the forces are equal, opposite and parallel.

rubric.why: The forces act along different lines and produce a turning effect.
rubric.description: States the separation of the forces and their rotational effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the separated lines of action and the resulting rotation or turning effect.

modelAnswer: A couple is a pair of equal, opposite and parallel forces acting along different lines.
It produces a turning effect or rotation.

items.followUp: Define work and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: The SI unit of work is the joule (J).
rubric.description: Names the SI unit of work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for joule or J.

rubric.why: One joule is the work done when a force of one newton moves an object one metre in the direction of the force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct force and displacement in the direction of the force.

modelAnswer: The SI unit of work is the joule (J).
One joule is the work done when a force of 1 N moves an object through 1 m in the direction of the force.

items.followUp: A body has a mass of 12 kg and a volume of 3 m³. Find its density.

rubric.why: Density is defined as mass per unit volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that density is mass per unit volume.

rubric.why: The SI unit is kilogram per cubic metre.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit of density.

modelAnswer: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance.
Its SI unit is kilogram per cubic metre (kg/m³).

items.followUp: What is the value of absolute zero in kelvin and degrees Celsius?

rubric.why: Absolute zero is the lowest possible temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the lowest possible temperature.

rubric.description: Gives the value of absolute zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 0 K or approximately −273 °C.

modelAnswer: Absolute zero is the lowest possible temperature, at which molecular motion is minimum.

items.followUp: Define the melting point of a pure substance.

rubric.why: At the melting point, a solid changes into a liquid; at the freezing point, a liquid changes into a solid.
rubric.description: Distinguishes the direction of the change of state.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the change of state for both processes.

rubric.why: For a pure substance at a fixed pressure, the melting point and freezing point are the same temperature.
rubric.description: States the relationship between the two temperatures.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying they are equal for a pure substance at the same pressure.

modelAnswer: At the melting point, a solid changes into a liquid; at the freezing point, a liquid changes into a solid.
For a pure substance at the same pressure, the melting point and freezing point are equal.

items.followUp: Why is rolling friction usually less than sliding friction?

rubric.why: Sliding friction acts when one surface slides over another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing friction between surfaces that slide over each other.

rubric.why: Rolling friction acts when an object rolls over a surface and is generally smaller than sliding friction.
rubric.description: Defines rolling friction and compares its size.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing rolling friction and stating that it is less than sliding friction.

modelAnswer: Sliding friction acts when one surface slides over another.
Rolling friction acts when an object rolls over a surface and is usually less than sliding friction.

items.followUp: If a bag weighs 30 N, what force must you apply to hold it stationary?

rubric.why: The force applied to hold the bag must act upward, opposite to its weight.
rubric.description: Gives the direction of the applied force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the force acts upward or opposite to gravity.

rubric.why: For the bag to remain stationary, the applied force must balance its weight.
rubric.description: Gives the magnitude condition for equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the force equals the bag's weight.

modelAnswer: Apply an upward force, opposite to the bag's weight.
To keep the bag stationary, the applied force must be equal to its weight.

items.followUp: State two ways friction is useful in everyday life.

rubric.why: Friction between our feet and the ground enables us to walk without slipping.
rubric.description: Gives one everyday advantage of friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example such as walking, writing or gripping objects.

rubric.why: Friction also makes activities such as writing, braking and holding objects possible.
rubric.description: Gives a second everyday advantage of friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid advantage distinct from the first example.

modelAnswer: Friction between our feet and the ground enables us to walk without slipping.
Friction between a pen and paper enables us to write.
